message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We compute the
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline1.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\text{Pin}(2)$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -equivariant Seiberg–Witten Floer homology of Seifert rational homology three-spheres in terms of their Heegaard Floer homology. As a result of this computation, we prove Manolescu’s conjecture that
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline2.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FD}=-\bar{\unicode[STIX]{x1D707}}$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    for Seifert integral homology three-spheres. We show that the Manolescu invariants
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline3.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FC},\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FD},$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline4.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FE}$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    give new obstructions to homology cobordisms between Seifert fiber spaces, and that many Seifert homology spheres
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline5.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6F4}(a_{1},\ldots ,a_{n})$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    are not homology cobordant to any
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline6.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$-\unicode[STIX]{x1D6F4}(b_{1},\ldots ,b_{n})$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . We then use the same invariants to give an example of an integral homology sphere not homology cobordant to any Seifert fiber space. We also show that the
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline7.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\text{Pin}(2)$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -equivariant Seiberg–Witten Floer spectrum provides homology cobordism obstructions distinct from
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline8.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FC},\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FD},$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline9.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\unicode[STIX]{x1D6FE}$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . In particular, we identify an
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" mimetype="image" xlink:href="S0010437X19007620_inline10.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$\mathbb{F}[U]$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -module called connected Seiberg–Witten Floer homology, whose isomorphism class is a homology cobordism invariant.
                  </jats:p>
title: Pin(2)-equivariant Seiberg–Witten Floer homology of Seifert fibrations
